Book: chapter-07.txt lines 505–510 (constancy of Θ on P_i ∖ {0}) is the source of the argument.

proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the domains V_i := ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_{j≠i} P_j), parts (i) and (ii) and the disjointness used in part (iii).
1. (Definition and openness.) Let F := ⋃_{j ∈ Fin q, j ≠ i} P_j and V := ℝ^P ∖ F. Each P_j is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). The index set {j ∈ Fin q | j ≠ i} is finite, so F is closed as a finite union of closed sets (Set.Finite.isClosed_biUnion). Hence V is open.
2. (P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V.) Let x ∈ P_i with x ≠ 0, and suppose x ∈ F. Then x ∈ P_j for some j ≠ i, so x ∈ P_i ⊓ P_j (Submodule.mem_inf). By hypothesis P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥, so x = 0 (Submodule.mem_bot), a contradiction. Hence x ∈ V.
3. (V is disjoint from P_j for j ≠ i.) For j ≠ i, P_j ⊆ F = ℝ^P ∖ V.
4. (V ∩ P_i is connected.) We distinguish two cases.
   Case (a): no j ∈ Fin q with j ≠ i exists. Then F = ∅ and V = ℝ^P, so V ∩ P_i = P_i. This set is convex (Submodule.convex) and nonempty (0 ∈ P_i), hence connected (Convex.isConnected).
   Case (b): some j ≠ i exists. Then 0 ∈ P_j ⊆ F, so 0 ∉ V; together with step 2, V ∩ P_i = P_i ∖ {0}.
   - Regard P_i as a real normed space with the induced norm. Its rank equals finrank P_i = 2 > 1 (Module.finrank_eq_rank).
   - By Mathlib's isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank, the set {0}ᶜ ⊆ P_i is connected.
   - The inclusion Subtype.val : P_i → ℝ^P is continuous, and it maps {0}ᶜ exactly onto P_i ∖ {0}: an element of P_i is nonzero iff its image is nonzero (Subtype.ext).
   So P_i ∖ {0} = V ∩ P_i is connected (IsConnected.image).
   Elementary alternative for case (b), which avoids importing Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected: take an orthonormal basis e₁, e₂ of P_i. The map (r, t) ↦ r(cos t·e₁ + sin t·e₂) is continuous on (0, ∞) × ℝ, which is convex and hence connected. It maps this set onto P_i ∖ {0}:
   - every image point lies in P_i and has norm r > 0;
   - a nonzero x = a e₁ + b e₂ ∈ P_i has z := a + b·i ≠ 0 in ℂ, and x = |z|(cos(arg z)·e₁ + sin(arg z)·e₂) by Complex.cos_arg and Complex.sin_arg.
5. Steps 1–4 show that V is open, V ∩ P_i is connected, P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V, and V is disjoint from P_j for every j ≠ i. ∎
Implementation note: isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected, which the frozen contract does not import. Either add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected` to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean (accepted candidates have added Mathlib imports before) or use the elementary alternative in step 4(b).
key_steps: Take V := ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_{j≠i} P_j; finite-dimensional subspaces are closed, so V is open.
P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V because P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥ for j ≠ i, and P_j ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ V for j ≠ i.
If no j ≠ i exists, V ∩ P_i = P_i is convex and nonempty, hence connected.
Otherwise 0 ∉ V, so V ∩ P_i = P_i ∖ {0}: the image of the connected set {0}ᶜ of the space P_i (rank 2 > 1, isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank) under the continuous inclusion.
